entries.claim: Task 1 defines the hostname check as a deny-list (refuse only `:`, `/`, `?`, `#`, `@`, `[`, `]` and whitespace), and that list still lets through hosts that make httpx raise when the 8088 client is built. So F-015 (a saved host that stops every later start) stays open.
entries.failure_scenario: Probed against the repo's httpx: `xn--zz` raises IDNAError, `a\x7fb` raises InvalidURL ('non-printable ASCII'), and `💥.local` raises InvalidURL ('Invalid IDNA hostname'). None of the three holds a listed character or whitespace, so the validator accepts them at the save. `apply_connection` then writes the record and `build_http_client` raises (500). Plan 3 Task 1 runs the same validator at read, so the record reads as valid, and `create_app`, which catches only StoreCorruptError, crashes on every start. Task 1's refuse cases include none of these, so its tests stay green. A positive LDH/IDNA check, or a validator that tries to build the URL, would close this; the plan's wording does not require either.

entries.claim: Task 6 adds a read of the stored record to the save path ('the one connection.json already held'), but no plan guards that read against a corrupt or invalid record. Plan 3 Task 1 makes only `remembered` tolerant of such a record, and nothing tests a save over one, so D-09's 'the file stays until the user saves over it' can fail.
entries.failure_scenario: connection.json holds `a:b` (refused by Plan 3 Task 1) or unparseable JSON. The app starts on the defaults (127.0.0.1). The user logs in and saves at 127.0.0.1 with the password blank and remember:true. Task 6's read of the stored password raises ConnectionStoreCorruptError, which renders as a 500 `store_corrupt`. The save that D-09 relies on to replace the file never succeeds. Plan 3 Task 1's Verify checks only /api/health and /api/login, so this path goes untested.

entries.claim: Task 2 handles the new invalid-host refusal only in `submitConnection`'s save path. `logIn`'s LOGIN_VERDICTS map knows only login_refused, login_not_answered and login_values_pinned, so the refusal Plan 1 Task 2 adds at /api/login is rethrown and nothing is shown.
entries.failure_scenario: A logged-out user types `a:b` and presses Save. Today check_pair catches InvalidURL and the panel shows 'HQPlayer did not answer.' After Plan 1 Task 2 the login answers the new code instead. `logIn` reaches `if (!next) throw e;`, the click handler `() => submitConnection(true)` does not catch it, and the static code has no unhandledrejection handler. The panel shows no report and the user does not learn why the login failed. AC2 refuses at login, but the user never sees the refusal.

entries.claim: After Task 3, Task 2's two proof tests pass whether or not the D-09 rule is in the code, and no later task re-asserts the rule with the marker on. The locked D-09 behavior (a corrupt or invalid record starts no alias probe) is then left without an automated check.
entries.failure_scenario: Task 2's tests build a Config with no marker, because the marker field does not exist yet. Task 3 then makes every unmarked start skip the probe. Both cases (unparseable JSON, `a:b`) now pass with the corrupt-record early return deleted. Task 3 reruns only the two named alias tests, and Task 5 tests marker-on with no record, never with a corrupt one. A regression that probes the alias over a corrupt record in the image therefore passes the suite. The DISPOSITIONS proof for this part of F-015 and F-022 is then a test that no longer fails on the defect.

entries.claim: Task 5 offers the alias only through a ConnectionReport field or the discovery answer. Both are gated reads (OPEN_PATHS is only /api/health and /api/login), so a fresh container install, which starts logged out, never sees the offer that D-04 requires and Task 6 renders.
entries.failure_scenario: Fresh Docker install, marker on, daemon on the host. Startup probes the alias and keeps it as an offer, but GET /api/connection and GET /api/discover both answer 401 to the logged-out panel. The offer never renders. The login sends no host, so it goes to 127.0.0.1 inside the container and fails with 'HQPlayer did not answer.' The only way forward is the existing static 'host.docker.internal' hint. Once logged in, the user is already connected, so the offer does nothing. Task 6's Verify feeds the offer to the store directly, so it never exercises the logged-out state.

entries.claim: Task 4's Verify requires every proof node id to be collected by `.venv/bin/pytest --collect-only`. F-021's fixing tests are JS tests (Plan 2 Task 1 in tests/js/store/setup.test.js and tests/js/components/chrome/setup.test.js), which pytest cannot collect, so the check cannot pass with a truthful F-021 entry.
entries.failure_scenario: The executor records `tests/js/store/setup.test.js` `test_discovery_...` as F-021's proof, and `pytest --collect-only -q` on that path fails. The executor must then either fail the task, or drop the JS proof and cite a Python test that does not prove the D-07 browser-side fix. The second weakens AC7's 'a proof test that fails against the pre-fix code' for F-021.

entries.claim: Task 3 makes the /log ceiling a refusal and asks for a value and basis 'as in Task 2'. But CONTEXT D-12 measured only forms and settings backups, the task does not ask for /log or /about to be measured, and it has no check that a log of realistic size still tails.
entries.failure_scenario: GET /log returns the daemon's whole log (logtail.fetch_log returns `resp.text`, and tail_text then keeps 256 KiB). A long-running hqplayerd log larger than the guessed ceiling is now refused outright, so the System-tab tail (`engineread.read_log_tail`) shows an error on a healthy daemon. Task 3's Verify checks only over-ceiling refusal and the drip, unlike Task 2's 'a body at the measured maximum passes', so the regression would ship.

entries.claim: Task 2 says its save cases will fail against the pre-change code because the build raised InvalidURL. In the default test client that is a raised exception, not an assertion failure, and docs/testing.md rule 8 counts only an assertion failure as proof of bite. Task 3 and Plan 3 Task 1 both say how to get an assertion failure; this task does not.
entries.failure_scenario: Before the change, POST /api/connection with `a:b` writes the record and then `httpx.AsyncClient(base_url='http://a:b:8088')` raises InvalidURL. The `Exception` handler renders a 500, but Starlette's ServerErrorMiddleware re-raises it, and the default TestClient (tests/support/apps.py `raise_server_exceptions=True`) raises it into the test. So the proof run ends in an error rather than an assertion failure, and the DISPOSITIONS proof for F-005 has not been shown to bite.

entries.claim: Task 1 lists `_adopt_alias` as one of `build_http_client`'s three callers. Plan 3 Task 5, which runs earlier, removes that call ('no longer writes cfg.hqp_host or rebuilds the 8088 client'), so the caller list is stale when Plan 4 runs.
entries.failure_scenario: The executor following Task 1 looks for a `build_http_client` call in `_adopt_alias` to thread the clock through and finds none. That either stalls the task or tempts the executor to reintroduce a rebuild there, which would contradict D-04 ('never written into cfg.hqp_host on its own').
